patients.summary: Retired long-haul trucker with alcoholic cirrhosis, alcohol pancreatitis, CAD with a stent and a 2013 pancreatic tail cancer, who quits drinking in 2021, develops a Zenker diverticulum and then a second pancreatic adenocarcinoma in the head with chronic DIC in 2022 treated by completion total pancreatectomy, then glucagon-deficiency hypoglycemia, decompensated cirrhosis, prostatitis and a 2026 ICU stay for aspiration pneumonia with euthyroid sick syndrome.

New patient visit booked 6/11 at 9:00, 60 min slot. Records release form sent with the packet; she will bring it signed so we can request his old chart and his cancer center records.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT
63 yo M establishing care, here with his wife. Last regular PCP retired in 2018. Records requested today.

HPI / background (per patient and wife, old records pending):
- Pancreatic cancer of the tail, 2013. Had a distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy at a regional cancer center. Says he was followed by oncology with scans for about five years and "they let me go" last year. Recalls getting a set of shots after the spleen came out.
- Alcohol-related chronic pancreatitis. On pancrelipase with meals for years; stools OK when he takes it, greasy when he skips it.
- Cirrhosis from alcohol. Told about it several years ago. No history of vomiting blood, belly swelling or confusion that he knows of. Uses lactulose now and then for constipation, not daily.
- CAD with a drug-eluting stent in 2016. No chest pain. On aspirin and atorvastatin. Doesn't have a cardiologist now.
- BPH on tamsulosin, gets up once a night, stream OK.

Alcohol: about 6 drinks a day (beer, some whiskey on weekends) for about 30 years. Knows it's what did his liver and pancreas. Wife is clearly worried. He is not ready to stop "yet". No withdrawal seizures or DTs.
Tobacco: 1 ppd since his mid 20s, roughly 37 pack-years. Has tried to quit cold turkey a couple of times.
Retired long-haul truck driver. Lives with wife in Leeds.

FHx: father - alcohol use disorder and cirrhosis. Mother - type 2 diabetes. Older brother - CAD, MI at 62.

Meds: tamsulosin 0.4 daily, aspirin 81 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, pancrelipase 36,000 lipase units with meals, MVI daily, lactulose 15 mL BID prn.
Allergies: none known.

ROS: no chest pain, no dyspnea beyond baseline, no melena, no abdominal swelling, no jaundice, appetite fine. Weight stable per him.

Exam: well appearing, smells of tobacco. Anicteric. No spider angiomata seen. Neck supple. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, mildly diminished at bases. Abdomen soft, nontender, old left upper quadrant and midline scars well healed, no fluid wave, liver edge not palpable. No asterixis. No edema.
AUDIT-C 10. PHQ-2 1.

A/P
1. Alcoholic cirrhosis, compensated by history. CMP, CBC, INR, GGT today. Liver US for surveillance. Hep A/B: no immunity records, start Twinrix today. HCV, HBsAg, HIV today.
2. Alcohol use disorder. Long talk. Not ready. Discussed that the liver and pancreas will keep paying for it. Left the door open; will revisit each visit.
3. Tobacco: 1 ppd. Advised to quit; not ready, will think about it. Low-dose CT lung screening ordered.
4. Chronic pancreatitis: continue pancrelipase.
5. CAD s/p stent: ECG today normal. Continue aspirin and atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
6. BPH: stable on tamsulosin.
7. Asplenia: will check old records for which vaccines he had in 2013 before giving more.
8. HM: Tdap today. Colonoscopy - says he had one last year, get records.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Mr. Simard,
Your labs are back. Your liver enzymes (AST, GGT) are up the way we see with regular drinking, and your bilirubin and albumin are close to normal, so the liver is still keeping up for now. Blood counts and clotting time are OK. Cholesterol is well controlled on the atorvastatin.
Hepatitis C, hepatitis B and HIV tests were all negative.
The best thing you can do for these numbers is cut back on alcohol. We'll keep talking about it.

reports.text: Liver: coarsened echotexture with nodular surface contour. No focal hepatic lesion. Portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow. Gallbladder normal, no stones. Common bile duct 4 mm. Pancreatic head and body partly obscured by bowel gas; pancreatic tail and spleen surgically absent. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. No ascites. Aorta normal caliber.
reports.conclusion: Cirrhotic morphology of the liver without focal lesion. No ascites. Postsurgical absence of the spleen.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Low-dose technique. Lungs clear without nodules, consolidation or effusion. Airways patent. Heart size normal; coronary stent noted. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen notable for postsurgical changes of splenectomy.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Imaging results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: US: cirrhotic liver, no mass, no fluid. CT chest: no nodules, Lung-RADS 1. Both repeat in a year. Letter mailed.

documents.title: Prior records abstract
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Records received from prior PCP office and cancer center (412 pages, scanned to media). Abstracted:
- 2013: adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic tail. Distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy. Oncology surveillance with CT scans through 2018, no recurrence, released from surveillance 2018.
- Post-splenectomy vaccines 2013: PCV13, MenACWY and Hib on 5/14/13, PPSV23 on 7/16/13. No record of MenB or a MenACWY booster since.
- 2016: PCI with drug-eluting stent at an outside cardiology group. Aspirin and atorvastatin after.
- Cirrhosis noted on cancer center imaging; labeled alcohol related. Pancreatitis on pancrelipase.
- Colonoscopy 2018: normal, repeat in 10 years.
- No allergies listed.
Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed abstract. Asplenia: MenACWY booster overdue (5 yr), MenB never given. Will give MenACWY + MenB #1 with Twinrix #2 next week. Pneumococcal series done 2013. Colonoscopy 2018 normal, next 2028.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for Twinrix #2, MenACWY booster and MenB #1 per PCP. VIS given, questions answered. Twinrix R deltoid, MenACWY L deltoid, MenB L deltoid lower. Tolerated well, observed 15 min. MenB #2 due in 1-2 months, Twinrix #3 due December. Scheduled.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Follow-up cirrhosis, pancreatitis, alcohol. Still drinking about the same, "maybe a little less on weekdays". Smoking 1 ppd. No abdominal swelling, no confusion, no black stools. Eating OK, taking enzymes with meals. Wife not with him today.
O: Vitals as charted. Anicteric. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no fluid wave. No asterixis. No edema.
A/P:
- Alcohol use disorder, still drinking. Discussed again, including options (counseling, groups, medications that are safe with his liver). Not interested today.
- Cirrhosis: repeat CMP/CBC.
- Tobacco: not ready.
- Flu shot and MenB #2 today.
RTC 4 mo.

documents.author: PCP

Here with wife. Holidays were "heavy", by his own report. Still 1 ppd. No new symptoms; denies abdominal swelling, jaundice, hematemesis or melena. Prostate symptoms unchanged.
Exam: NAD. Anicteric, no palmar erythema. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen soft, nontender, no ascites. No edema. No asterixis.
Labs today. Wife asks what happens if he keeps drinking - honest answer given (liver failure is the likely road). He listened. Says he'll "try cutting back after the Super Bowl".
Continue current meds. RTC April.

Feels fine. Weight on home scale 181 lb. Still drinking daily. Smokes on the porch, 1 ppd. Pancrelipase working. No new urinary issues. No chest pain with yard work.
Appears well on video, anicteric to the extent visible, speaking full sentences.
Plan: in-person wellness visit in July with labs. Encouraged him to set a quit date for either cigarettes or alcohol; he says "one thing at a time, maybe the beer". Will follow.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT (initial)
Health risk assessment reviewed with pt and wife. Independent in ADLs/IADLs. Drives locally. No falls. Hearing OK, uses readers. Lives with wife.
Functional/cognitive screen: oriented, recalls 3/3.
PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 10 - still about 6 drinks daily.
Tobacco 1 ppd. Counseled again; still not ready.
Advance directives: wife is health care proxy, will bring a copy of the form.

Problems reviewed: cirrhosis (compensated), alcohol-related chronic pancreatitis, CAD s/p stent 2016, BPH, hx pancreatic tail cancer 2013 s/p distal pancreatectomy/splenectomy, asplenia, alcohol use disorder.
Meds reconciled, no changes.
Exam: anicteric, lungs clear, RRR, abdomen soft without ascites, no edema.

Prevention plan:
- LDCT lung screening due - ordered.
- Liver US - ordered.
- Colonoscopy 2018 normal.
- Vaccines: Twinrix series done; MenACWY/MenB done 2019; Tdap 2019. Shingrix and flu in the fall.
- Labs today.
Written plan given.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Comparison 7/2/2019. Lungs clear without nodules or consolidation. No effusion. Heart normal size; coronary stent. No adenopathy. Splenectomy changes in the upper abdomen.

Liver nodular in contour with coarse echotexture, unchanged. No focal lesion. Portal vein patent with normal direction of flow. Gallbladder unremarkable. CBD 4 mm. Spleen surgically absent. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Stable cirrhotic liver without focal lesion. No ascites.

documents.title: Imaging results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your lung screening CT was clear, and the liver ultrasound shows the same cirrhosis pattern as last year with no growths and no fluid. Both get repeated next summer. The lung CT is a good reason to keep thinking about the cigarettes.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Masked visit, wife present. She is frank today: he is drinking every day, she is scared about his liver after watching his father. He agrees he "needs to do something" and asks whether he can stop on his own. Never had withdrawal symptoms on days he didn't drink. Smoking 1 ppd.
No GI bleeding, no swelling, no confusion.
Exam: anicteric, lungs clear, RRR, abdomen soft without ascites, no asterixis, no tremor.
A/P: AUD - first real readiness. Talked through a plan to taper and stop, warning signs of withdrawal, and support (groups, counseling referral offered). He wants to try on his own after the holidays. Wife on board. Call us if shaky or sweating when he cuts down.
Labs today. Shingrix #2 2 weeks.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Big news - stopped drinking about 2.5 weeks ago, first week of February. Tapered over a few days in late January the way we discussed, then stopped. Some poor sleep the first week, no shakes, no sweats, no hallucinations. Wife poured out what was in the house. Doing it on his own with her help. Still smoking 1 ppd - "can't do both at once".
No abdominal swelling, no jaundice, no bleeding.
O: Vitals as charted. Calm, no tremor. Anicteric. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen soft without ascites. No asterixis.
A/P:
- Alcohol use disorder, early abstinence. Congratulated him. Reviewed relapse plan; he knows he can call. Medication support discussed; he prefers to keep going without one for now.
- Cirrhosis: labs today, expect the enzymes to settle over the next months.
- Tobacco: will revisit once sobriety feels steady.
RTC June for wellness visit.

orders.reason: progressive dysphagia with regurgitation and weight loss

documents.title: Office Visit - dysphagia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: trouble swallowing.
HPI: About 5 months of food and drinks "hanging up" at the top of his throat, getting worse. Coughs during meals. Wife says his breath has been bad and he brings up chewed food that wasn't digested, mostly at night; a few times he has woken up choking. Feels a fullness in his neck that gurgles if he presses on it. Weight down about 11 lb since summer. No hematemesis, no melena, no odynophagia. Still sober (11 months). Smoking 1 ppd.
Exam: weight as charted, down 5 kg from last visit. Oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no mass or adenopathy palpable today. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen soft, no ascites.
A/P: Progressive oropharyngeal-type dysphagia with regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis and a gurgling neck - picture fits a pharyngoesophageal (Zenker) pouch; also need to exclude a stricture or mass given smoking and weight loss. GI referral, they will likely start with a barium swallow. Soft foods, upright after meals, eat slowly. Return precautions if he can't keep liquids down.

documents.title: GI appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: GI office scheduled consult 2/25 at 1:30; barium swallow same day. Wife informed.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology - consultation letter
Date of visit: 02/25/2022
Re: Vernon Simard, DOB 01/19/1956

Thank you for referring Mr. Simard, a 66-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis and chronic pancreatitis, for dysphagia.

He describes six months of steadily worsening difficulty getting down both solids and liquids, coughing with meals, bad breath, and regurgitation of undigested food, especially at night. His wife reports he sometimes wakes choking. He has lost about 5 kg. He notes a sense of fullness in the neck that gurgles with pressure.

Medications: tamsulosin, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, pancrelipase with meals, multivitamin, lactulose as needed. Allergies: none known.
Social: no current alcohol use.

Exam: unremarkable, including the neck.

Barium esophagram today: a posterior outpouching arising just above the upper esophageal sphincter, consistent with a Zenker diverticulum. No stricture or mass.

Impression: Zenker diverticulum, symptomatic.
Plan: flexible endoscopic diverticulotomy; we will schedule with our endoscopy unit. Soft diet in the meantime.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: Throat procedure
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Denise here. Vernon had the scope procedure for the pouch on Thursday (3/24). They kept him a few hours and sent him home on liquids, now soft food. Already he says things go down better and no choking at night so far. GI said follow up with them as needed. Just letting you know.

documents.title: RE: Throat procedure
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thank you for the update, glad it went well. Keep to soft foods as long as GI advised. He's due to see the doctor in May.

documents.title: Office Visit - jaundice
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, not eating, turning yellow.
HPI: Seen about 3 months after GI found the Zenker diverticulum; swallowing much better since the March procedure. Now 2 months of fatigue, poor appetite and about 20 lb of weight loss. Wife noticed over the last week that his skin looks "pale yellow". Occasional nausea and a vague upper belly discomfort that doesn't change with eating or bowel movements. No fever, no vomiting, no change in bowel habits. No dark stools.
Alcohol: none since February 2021, confirmed by wife.
Tobacco: still 1 ppd, has smoked about 40 years.
Hx: pancreatic tail adenocarcinoma 2013 s/p distal pancreatectomy/splenectomy; cirrhosis; alcohol pancreatitis; CAD s/p stent.

Exam: weight 68 kg (77 in January). Mild scleral icterus. No spider angiomata. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen: fullness in the epigastrium without tenderness, no palpable mass, no ascites. No asterixis. No edema.

A/P:
1. New jaundice with weight loss in a man with prior pancreatic cancer and cirrhosis. Progressive jaundice with weight loss - worried about a pancreatic or biliary process before blaming the liver. Hepatic panel, CBC, INR, BMP today. CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast this week (got it on the schedule for Thursday).
2. Unintentional weight loss - as above.
3. Tobacco use disorder - 1 ppd x 40 yrs. Strongly advised to stop now. Offered patch/varenicline; he wants to quit on his own, "same way I did the booze".
Discussed the reason for urgency with him and his wife.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cholestatic pattern: alk phos ~290, bili 3.0 (direct 2.2), AST/ALT mildly up. INR stable. Keeps CT Thursday. Called pt.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Indication: painless jaundice, weight loss, prior distal pancreatectomy.
Pancreas: postsurgical absence of the pancreatic body-tail. Hypoenhancing mass in the pancreatic head measuring 2.6 x 2.2 cm. Mild biliary ductal dilation upstream of the mass.
Liver: nodular contour consistent with known cirrhosis; no focal lesion.
Spleen: surgically absent.
Gallbladder unremarkable without stones. Adrenals and kidneys normal; no hydronephrosis.
No ascites. No enlarged abdominal or pelvic lymph nodes. Aorta normal in caliber.
Bowel unremarkable. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: 2.6 cm mass in the pancreatic head with mild biliary dilation, concerning for malignancy. Cirrhotic liver without focal lesion.

orders.order: Gastroenterology referral for endoscopic ultrasound with biopsy
orders.reason: pancreatic head mass with biliary dilation

documents.title: CT result discussed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt and wife with CT: mass in the head of the pancreas, about 2.6 cm, blocking the bile duct a little. Liver looks like his known cirrhosis with no spots. Told them plainly this is worrying for a new pancreatic cancer and needs a biopsy. Spoke with GI directly; EUS with biopsy next Friday 5/27. Wife asked about the 2013 cancer - may be a recurrence or a new one, the biopsy will help. They will call with any fever or pain.

procedures.procedure: Endoscopic ultrasound with fine-needle biopsy of pancreatic mass

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of head of pancreas

reports.text:
Specimen: pancreas, head mass, EUS-guided fine-needle biopsy.
Microscopic: fragments of gland-forming malignant epithelium with intracellular and extracellular mucin production.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head, mucin-producing.

documents.title: Biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pathology back: adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head, mucin-producing. Called and discussed with pt and wife, both on speaker. He was quiet, wife had questions about whether he is a surgical candidate - that's the oncology/surgery conversation, referral sent today to the cancer center, asked for an expedited new patient visit. Will stay involved. He says he is cutting down and means to quit.

documents.title: Oncology and cigarettes
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, Denise again. Cancer center called, his first appointment is June 21. Also he really did quit, last cigarette was May 28 and he threw out the cartons. He's cranky but doing it. Is there anything he should be eating? He has no appetite.

documents.title: RE: Oncology and cigarettes
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's a big deal - please tell him I said so. For now: small meals often, protein at each one (eggs, yogurt, shakes), take the enzymes with every meal and snack. The cancer center has a dietitian; ask for a visit on the 21st.

documents.title: Oncology visit update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called after his cancer center visit 6/21. More scans and blood tests ordered there, plan to be decided by their team; back to see oncology in August. No note received yet - requested. Still not smoking. Eating a little more. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PA renewal - pancrelipase
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Annual PA renewal for pancrelipase 36,000 completed (chronic pancreatitis, pancreatic insufficiency, s/p distal pancreatectomy). Approved 1 yr.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Fasting labs drawn first. Here with wife.
Still losing weight, now 62 kg. Very tired, naps most afternoons. Appetite poor. Still yellow. Upper belly ache on and off, no fever or vomiting. Not smoking since 5/28. Not drinking. Oncology follow-up is 8/18.
Exam: thin, jaundiced. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric fullness, no ascites. No edema.
A/P: weight loss and persistent jaundice with pancreatic head cancer, awaiting oncology plan. Labs today including fasting glucose and A1c. With this much weight loss and a pancreatic tumor, checking for diabetes. Will send results to oncology before 8/18. Nutrition as discussed; supplement shakes.

medications.drug_text: 3 ML insulin glargine 100 UNT/ML Pen Injector
medications.sig: Inject 10 units under the skin at bedtime

documents.title: Results - diabetes
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt and wife. Fasting glucose 176, A1c 7.8% - new diabetes. Explained it often shows up with a pancreatic tumor, on top of his prior partial pancreatectomy and chronic pancreatitis. Given his cirrhosis and ongoing weight loss, starting basal insulin rather than pills: glargine 10 units at bedtime. Meter, strips, pen needles sent. RN teaching visit Tuesday. Check fasting sugars daily; call if under 70 or over 300. Lows reviewed (shaky, sweaty, confused - treat with juice).
Bilirubin 3.6, alk phos higher than May, platelets 118, INR 1.4 - faxed to oncology for the 18th.

documents.title: Insulin teaching
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 45 min teaching with pt and wife. Glargine pen: priming, dialing, abdomen/thigh sites, rotating. Pt gave first dose with return demonstration (saline practice). Meter set up, wife will log readings. Hypoglycemia signs and treatment (4 oz juice or 4 glucose tabs, recheck in 15 min). Sick-day basics. Teach-back good. Wife says she'll keep juice boxes in the truck and by the bed.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology - clinic letter
Visit date: 08/18/2022
Patient: Vernon Simard, DOB 01/19/1956

Mr. Simard, 66, returns to our clinic. He is known to us for a 2013 pancreatic tail adenocarcinoma resected by distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy, and now has a biopsy-proven mucin-producing adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head. He also has alcohol-related chronic pancreatitis and cirrhosis.

He reports ongoing fatigue and about 15 lb of weight loss over the last three months, without any change in diet or activity. His primary care physician recently diagnosed diabetes (fasting glucose 176 mg/dL, HbA1c 7.8%) and started basal insulin.
Former smoker, about 40 pack-years, quit in May. Former heavy drinker, abstinent since early 2021. Retired truck driver.

Exam: jaundiced. Mild tenderness in the epigastrium.
Liver tests: bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase elevated.
Abdominal ultrasound: dilated common bile duct; no gallstones.
Coagulation studies: platelets low, fibrinogen low, D-dimer elevated, INR mildly prolonged. In this setting we read this as a chronic, low-grade disseminated intravascular coagulation related to the tumor. No bleeding or clots.

Assessment: mucin-producing adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head with chronic DIC; biliary obstruction.
Plan: ERCP with biliary stent next week. Once the bilirubin falls, neoadjuvant gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel, then restaging and surgical review for completion pancreatectomy. We will follow his counts and coagulation closely.

Medications reviewed: insulin glargine 10 units at bedtime, tamsulosin, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, pancrelipase with meals, multivitamin, lactulose as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Outside endocrinology - consultation
Seen 02/13/2023
Patient: Vernon Simard, 67 M

Reason: low blood sugars after total pancreatectomy.
Six weeks ago he had a completion total pancreatectomy for a pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, after a 2013 distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy. Diabetes was diagnosed last August and he has used insulin injections since.
For the past month he has had episodes several times a week, a few hours after meals, of shakiness, anxiety and palpitations that settle quickly with juice or a snack. His wife sees him sweaty, irritable and briefly confused during them. He is hungrier between meals and has lost another 5 lb. Good adherence; keeps all appointments. No fever, chest pain or recent illness.
History: alcohol-related cirrhosis and chronic pancreatitis, CAD with stent, BPH. Former smoker (about 40 pack-years), quit in May 2022. No alcohol since early 2021. Retired truck driver.
Family: mother with type 2 diabetes.
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime; insulin lispro sliding scale with meals; tamsulosin 0.4 mg; aspirin 81 mg; atorvastatin 40 mg; pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals; multivitamin; lactulose 15 mL BID prn. NKDA.
Exam: well-healing midline scar. Neuro nonfocal. Heart, lungs and abdomen normal.

Assessment: post-pancreatectomy hypoglycemia with loss of glucagon counter-regulation, in insulin-requiring diabetes after total pancreatectomy.
Plan:
- Lower the lispro correction scale (new scale given); skip lispro if he eats less than half a meal.
- Smaller, more frequent meals with protein; bedtime snack.
- Glucose tablets on him at all times; glucagon nasal powder 3 mg prescribed for severe lows, wife taught.
- Continue glargine 24 units for now.
- Return in 3 months with meter download.
Endocrinology

Regional hospital - discharge summary (abbreviated)
Admitted 02/19/2026 via ED to ICU. Discharged 03/12/2026 to a skilled nursing facility.
Patient: Vernon Simard, 70 M

Presentation: found unresponsive at home by his wife. Intubated on arrival for airway protection; IV fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics for presumed aspiration pneumonia. Needed low-dose vasopressors early; heart rate in the 90s; afebrile.
Background: Zenker diverticulum (treated 2022), pancreatic adenocarcinoma s/p completion total pancreatectomy, alcohol-related cirrhosis, insulin-treated diabetes, CAD s/p PCI with stent, BPH.
ICU course: over 10 days the pneumonia improved but he remained lethargic and ventilator dependent. Off sedation he moved little, opened eyes only to deep sternal rub, did not respond to voice, withdrew to pain; pupils equal and reactive; reflexes slow; no goiter, exophthalmos or tremor. Nutrition: mildly underweight. Encephalopathy labs: low serum albumin; thyroid tests with low total T3, normal T4 and normal TSH. No known thyroid or pituitary disease. Read as euthyroid sick syndrome (non-thyroidal illness) - no thyroid treatment; repeat thyroid tests after recovery.
Mental status improved steadily over the following week. Extubated 03/03, out of the ICU 03/05. Worked with PT/OT. Cause of the initial unresponsive episode not established.
Diagnoses: aspiration pneumonia; acute metabolic encephalopathy, resolving; euthyroid sick syndrome.
Discharge medications: home regimen resumed - insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro sliding scale with meals, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals, multivitamin, lactulose 15 mL BID prn. NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week of SNF discharge; repeat TSH/free T4/T3 in 6 weeks.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Denise called. Found him yesterday morning not waking up in bed, called 911. He's in the ICU at the regional hospital on a breathing machine; they think he aspirated. I spoke with the ICU team: pneumonia being treated, too early to say more. Gave them his history and our list; asked them to send records. Will call her later this week.

documents.title: SNF call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Skilled nursing facility nurse called: admitted yesterday from the hospital for rehab. Requested our med list and recent labs - faxed. Discharge summary to follow from the hospital. Expected stay 2-3 weeks.

documents.title: Home from rehab
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called: home yesterday (4/2) from the rehab facility. Walking with supervision, eating better. Home health PT and nursing referral sent by the facility, first visit Monday. TCM visit booked 4/7. Meds same as before the hospital per SNF list - reviewed by phone.

events.reason: transitional care after hospital and rehab

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Hospital 2/19-3/12 (ICU, intubated, aspiration pneumonia, prolonged encephalopathy, euthyroid sick picture on thyroid tests), then SNF rehab to 4/2. Discharge summary reviewed. Cause of being found unresponsive never established.
Now: alert, conversational, back to his usual self per wife. Weak; walks with supervision, home PT twice a week. Eating 5 small meals, enzymes with each. No cough, no fever, swallowing OK for soft solids and thin liquids. Sugars 120s-240s, no lows since home.
Exam: weight 55.5 kg (BMI about 18). Thin. Alert and oriented x3, normal speech. Faint icterus. Lungs clear, no crackles. RRR. Abdomen soft, no ascites. No edema. Gait slow but steady.
A/P:
1. Aspiration pneumonia - resolved. Encephalopathy - resolved.
2. Euthyroid sick syndrome - repeat TSH/free T4/free T3 in 3 weeks, about 6 weeks after discharge as the hospital asked.
3. Underweight after a long illness, low albumin - calorie/protein plan, shakes between meals.
4. Diabetes: continue glargine 24 + lispro scale; wife to log.
5. Cirrhosis: CMP/CBC today.
Med rec complete, no changes.

documents.title: Thyroid tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH, free T4 and free T3 all normal. The low T3 in the ICU was the illness, not his thyroid - euthyroid sick resolved. No further thyroid testing needed. Portal message sent.

documents.title: Home PT done
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Denise here. Home PT signed off last week, he walks to the mailbox and back twice a day. Weight on our scale is 123. Eating good. Anything else he needs before June?

documents.title: RE: Home PT done
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great progress. Nothing extra - keep the meals and snacks going. We'll weigh him and check labs at the June visit.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Recovered well from the winter admission. Walks daily, no falls, independent in ADLs again; wife does IADLs. PHQ-2 1. Sober 5 years, smoke-free 4.
ACP revisited after the ICU stay (20 min): his wishes unchanged - full treatment if recovery to home is likely, no long-term machines. He'd like to complete a MOLST at the next visit with his wife. HCP wife.
Exam: weight 56.5. Faint icterus. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen soft without ascites. Feet: intact sensation, pulses palpable, no lesions.
Plan: lipids, urine microalbumin. Liver ultrasound due. Eye exam in the fall. Fall vaccines.

reports.text: Comparison 4/8/2025. Nodular cirrhotic liver without focal lesion. Portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow. No biliary dilation. Pancreas and spleen surgically absent. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Stable cirrhotic liver, no focal lesion, no ascites.

documents.title: Ultrasound
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver US unchanged, no lesion, no ascites. Letter mailed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Summer check. Weight 57, slowly up. Energy better, walking further. No urinary symptoms. No cough or choking with meals. Sugars 110s-230s, a couple of mild lows after big lunches, treated with tabs. Endocrinology kept the same doses in July per pt. Oncology surveillance in July clear per pt.
Exam: faint icterus. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen soft, no ascites. No edema.
A/P: CMP, INR, A1c today. Continue current regimen. RTC late September; flu/COVID then.
